title: Pump Motor Overload
fullDescription: ER1 on Aquabot robotic cleaners indicates the pump motor draws excessive current. Common causes are clogged filter bag, debris in impeller, or motor wear.

title: Drive Motor Fault
fullDescription: ER2 indicates drive motor cannot move robot, often debris in track gears or worn brushes.

title: Out of Water Condition
fullDescription: ER3 means the cleaner senses no water flow. Submerge the unit and ensure it is properly bled of air.

title: Cable Communication Lost
shortDescription: Power supply lost contact with robot.
fullDescription: ER4 indicates the floating cable signal is lost. Inspect connector and cable jacket for damage.

title: Power Supply Internal Fault
fullDescription: ER5 indicates the supply unit detected a fault. Replace if persistent.

title: Power Supply Overheat
fullDescription: ER6 indicates the power supply has exceeded thermal limit. Move to shade.

title: Mains Voltage Fault
fullDescription: ER7 indicates voltage too high or low at the supply.

title: Scrubbing Brush Motor Stalled
fullDescription: ER8 indicates the scrubber brushes are stalled, often by hair or debris wrapping the brush.

title: Internal Sensor Fault
fullDescription: ER9 indicates a sensor reading invalid value. Service required if persistent.

title: Firmware Error
fullDescription: ER10 indicates firmware fault. Cycle power and update if available.
